extract: The Broken Shore, originally known as Thal'dranath, is where the Tomb of Sargeras - and thus the Burning Legion's gateway into Azeroth - is located. Gul'dan raised this island up from the bottom of the sea during the Second War, and it served as the demonic army's base of operations during the third invasion of the Burning Legion.

Above everything looms the dreaded Tomb of Sargeras, an ancient night elf temple that serves as the Legion's gateway into the world.|''[[The Art of World of Warcraft: Legion]]'', pg. 91}} '''The Broken Shore''', originally known as '''Thal'dranath''',[[The Tomb of Sargeras#Part One: The Fate of Another]]''[[Exploring Azeroth: Islands and Isles]]'', pg. 25 is where the [[Tomb of Sargeras]] - and thus the [[Burning Legion]]'s gateway into [[Azeroth]] - is located. [[Gul'dan]] raised this island up from the bottom of the sea during the [[Second War]],[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qrIdxNSreb0 Blizzcon 2015 | Alex Afrasiabi Legion behind the scenes!!][https://twitter.com/DaveKosak/status/694615640427003904 Dave Kosak on Twitter]: "The Tomb of Sargeras was raised. Other parts of the Broken Isles in Legion expansion have been around since the Sundering." and it served as the demonic army's base of operations during the [[third invasion of the Burning Legion]]. ==History== Ten thousand years ago, the Broken Shore, or Thal'dranath, was a portion of the city of [[Suramar City|Suramar]], and the location of the [[Temple of Elune]], which was built upon a site of ancient power.[[Chamber of the Moon#Quotes]] During the [[Great Sundering]], it was sent to the bottom of the oceans along with the majority of [[Kalimdor (landmass)|ancient Kalimdor]]'s landmass, as it was situated outside the boundaries of the shield raised by [[Grand Magistrix Elisande]]'s [[Highborne]]. Millennia later, the Guardian [[Aegwynn]] imprisoned the [[Avatar of Sargeras]] in the old temple, believing that its secret location down beneath the sea would be a perfect hiding place, along with the [[Eye of Sargeras|Eye]] and the [[Jeweled Scepter of Sargeras|Scepter of Sargeras]]. The corruptive energies of the Avatar of Sargeras would eventually warp its form with [[fel]] magic, turning it into the [[Tomb of Sargeras]].{{Ref WoWCV1|103|150}} ===Second War=== [[File:Chronicle2 Gul'dan and the Tomb of Sargeras.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Gul'dan]] raises the [[Tomb of Sargeras]].]] During the [[Second War]] in 6 [[ADP]], [[Gul'dan]] abandoned the [[Old Horde|Orcish Horde]] and led his [[Stormreaver clan|Stormreaver]] and [[Twilight's Hammer]] followers to the Broken Isles, seeking the power of the Tomb for himself. Using his experience raising the [[Hand of Gul'dan (subzone)|Hand of Gul'dan volcano]] from the ground of [[Shadowmoon Valley]],''[[Tides of Darkness]]'', chapter 17 the [[warlock]] led his men in raising the Shore from the bottom of the sea. As he opened the Tomb, [[Gul'dan]] was torn to shreds by the [[demon]]s [[Tomb Guardians|inside]]. [[Orgrim Doomhammer|Doomhammer]] loyalists of the [[Blackrock clan|Blackrock]] and [[Black Tooth Grin clan]]s then finished Gul'dan's troops,[[The Tomb of Sargeras (WC2 Orc)]] though the Hammer and [[Cho'gall]] managed to survive and escape. The orcs killed during the battle were eventually raised by the vile magics of the demons,[[The Tomb of Sargeras (WC2x Orc)]] and kept reliving it in their undeath. Forces later sent by [[Ner'zhul]] recovered the [[Jeweled Scepter of Sargeras]] from a demon,''[[Beyond the Dark Portal]]'', pg. 171-174 as he wanted to use it to escape the dying world of [[Draenor]] and eventually conquer other worlds. ===Third War=== {{WC3-section}} After the [[Third War]] in 21 [[ADP]], [[Illidan Stormrage]] entered the Tomb and recovered the [[Eye of Sargeras]]. Pursued by [[Maiev Shadowsong]] and her [[Warden]]s, he attempted to collapse part of the Temple on them for attempting to stop him from destroying the [[Lich King]], and for trying to imprison him once more.[[The Broken Isles (Warcraft III)]] ===Legion=== {{Legion-section}} [[File:Felstorm - Legion cinematic.png|thumb|left|The [[Felstorm]] above the Broken Shore.]] After the [[war in Draenor]] in 31 ADP, [[Gul'dan (alternate universe)|alternate Gul'dan]], guided by his master [[Kil'jaeden]]'s voice, managed to re-open the portal within the Tomb of Sargeras, ushering in the largest invasion of Azeroth by the [[Burning Legion]] since the [[War of the Ancients]]. Their ultimate goal was to finally summon the dark titan himself, [[Sargeras]], to Azeroth.[[The Tomb of Sargeras]] A massive army was sent by the forces of [[Azeroth]] to combat the Burning Legion in 32 ADP, including but not limited to the [[Alliance]], the [[Horde]], and the [[Argent Crusade]]. The [[Battle for the Broken Shore]] culminated in the Legion overrunning Azeroth's defenders and forcing them to withdraw. Many of the greatest heroes in Azeroth, such as [[Tirion Fordring]], [[Vol'jin]], and [[Varian Wrynn]], fell in battle before the Legion or were mortally wounded.[[The Battle for Broken Shore (quest)]] Some escaped, others went missing or were captured, but many more died upon the Broken Shore. A paladin [[adventurer|hero]] would return to the Broken Shore sometime after the disastrous battle to try and save [[Tirion Fordring]], who was held captive by the Legion and had lost the [[Ashbringer]]. The Ashbringer was reclaimed and used to battle [[Balnazzar]], who escaped before he could be defeated. On his deathbed, Tirion proclaimed the hero as the new wielder of the Ashbringer, before passing away.[[The Search for the Highlord]] The [[Knights of the Silver Hand|Order of the Silver Hand]] also sent their troops here, as the Broken Shore was littered with debris from battle, to gather plenty of [[Lumenstone]] despite the demons still patrolling the area.[[Lumenstone: Broken Shore (paladin)]] They also sent troops to help an order of [[priest]]s from the [[Conclave]] who have been spotted combing the landing site of the Broken Shore, searching for survivors amidst dangerous [[demon]]s, among them [[Temptress Salacia]] engaged in a battle with the priests and taken down by the paladins who joined the fray.[[The Highlord's Command: Holy Allies]] At some point, the champions of the [[Uncrowned]] investigated the area in search of [[Mathias Shaw]], and eventually encountered [[Belazius]] and his [[Felguard Legionnaire (Legion)|Felguard Legionnaires]].[[Where In the World is Mathias?: Obvious Start]] A [[demon hunter]] hero ventured to the Broken Shore to reclaim the [[Aldrachi Warblades]] from [[Caria Felsoul]], a traitor to the [[Illidari]].[[Vengeance Will Be Ours]] A [[warrior]] hero fought alongside many [[vrykul]] on the Broken Shore but was overwhelmed. They were saved from the brink of death by a [[val'kyr]] sent by Keeper [[Odyn]] and brought to the [[Halls of Valor]]. [[Vereesa Windrunner]] and a [[hunter]] hero, seeking Vereesa's missing sister [[Alleria Windrunner|Alleria]], used the Broken Shore as a launch point onto the Legion world of [[Niskara]] where Alleria was rumored to be held. [[Knights of the Ebon Blade]] launched a separate expedition to Niskara in order to locate [[Gorelix the Fleshripper]] in order to recover another artifact that was held in his hands. ====Legionfall==== [[File:ToS Trailer Legion Ship.png|thumb|[[Legion ship]]s warping above the Tomb of Sargeras.]] The demonic forces of the Burning Legion built massive structures on the Broken Shore as a base of operations for their assault on [[Azeroth]]. It's here that the Horde and the Alliance experienced a series of tragedies at the hands of the Legion. Where factions failed, order halls regrouped, acquired new weapons of power, and recruited new allies to make a triumphant return. All order halls gathered together to form the [[Armies of Legionfall]]. The Legionfall base, serving as the initial foothold on the island, is from where they would work their way through the Legion's defenses and eventually reach the stronghold. To do this, [[Class Order|class orders]] needed to work together to build up their forces by fortifying ancient elven buildings and upgrading them into Nether Disruptors, Command Centers, and Mage Towers.https://worldofwarcraft.com/en-us/news/20355988/world-of-warcraft-legion-what-s-next-panel-recap The destruction of [[Mephistroth]]'s [[Legion ship]] and its resulting crash into the Broken Shore heavily changes the center of the island's geography, destroying the fel lava pit and causing rubble from the ship to scatter across the area. ===Exploring Azeroth=== {{Novel-section}} Of anywhere on the [[Broken Isles]], the Broken Shore has experienced the most change by the Year 42 ADP. Its transformation at the hands of [[druid]]s and [[shaman]] is marked. Its waters are clear, hardy plants and flowers cover the ground, and the air is clean.''[[Exploring Azeroth: Islands and Isles]]'', pg. 23 The [[Tomb of Sargeras]] no longer glowed sickly from within, but there was still an air of darkness to it. It was guarded by the [[Watchers]], and the [[Image of Aegwynn|Echo of Aegwynn]] inside became more active. ==Geography== ===Maps and subregions=== [[File:VZ-Broken Shore.jpg|thumb|left|Map of the Broken Shore.]] {| class="darktable hlist" |- | *[[Aalgen Point]] *[[Black City|The Black City]] *[[Broken Valley]] *[[Cinder Run]] *[[Coal Ridge]] *[[Coast of Anguish]] *[[Crescent Ruins]] *[[Creeping Grotto|The Creeping Grotto]] **[[Blood Nest]] *[[Dark Stockades]] *''[[Darkspear's Might]]'' *[[Darkstone Isle]] *[[Deadwood Landing]] *[[Deliverance Point]] **[[Command Center (Broken Shore)|Command Center]] **[[Mage Tower (Broken Shore)|Mage Tower]] **[[Nether Disruptor]] *[[Felbreach Hollow]] *[[Feldust Cavern]] *[[Felfire Pass]] *[[Felrage Strand]] **[[Strand's End]] *[[Forlorn Depths]] *[[Foulshore Strip]] *[[Garrison of the Fel]] *[[Hijacked Portal|The Hijacked Portal]] **[[Bybeen Lair]] **[[Legion Command Ship]] **''[[Dreadex|The Dreadex]]'' **''[[The Dreadsoul]]'' *''[[Lion's Oath]]'' *[[Impsorrow Approach]] *[[Infernal Causeway]] *[[Jagged Cove]] *[[Lost Temple|The Lost Temple]] **[[Moonlight Ascent]] *[[Path of Suffering]] *[[Scavenger's Edge]] *[[Screaming Cliffs]] *[[Shadow Fracture]] *[[Shattered Edge|The Shattered Edge]] *[[Soldier's Torment]] **[[Pit of Agony|The Pit of Agony]] **[[Secret Treasure Lair]] *[[Soul Ruin]] *[[Stonefin Shoals]] *[[Tomb Approach]] *[[Tomb of Sargeras]] *[[Twisted Grounds|The Twisted Grounds]] *[[Veiled Isles|The Veiled Isles]] **{{ClassIcon|DeathKnight}} [[Acherus: The Ebon Hold]] *[[Vengeance Point]] *[[Weeping Terrace|The Weeping Terrace]] *[[Wrynnfall]] |- || ---- ;[[Lore location]]s *[[Chamber of the Eye]] |- || ---- ;{{WC3FT-inline}} [[Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne|Warcraft III]] *[[Brewmaster drinking area]] (presumed) *[[Izal-Shurah]] (presumed) |} {{clear|left}} VZ-Broken Shore-old.jpg|Broken Shore 7.0 map. Once players accept the relevant part of [[The Battle for Broken Shore (quest)]], they are teleported into a [[scenario]] version of the Broken Shore together with other players. ===Alliance perspective=== {{main|The Battle for Broken Shore (Alliance)}} ===Horde perspective=== {{main|The Battle for Broken Shore (Horde)}} ==Notes and trivia== [[File:WarCraftII-TidesOfDarkness-Orcs-Mission12-TombOfSargeras.png|thumb|upright|The island during the [[Second War]].]] *In ''[[Warcraft II: Beyond the Dark Portal|Beyond the Dark Portal]]'', a [[Dalaran (kingdom)|Dalaran]] expedition was depicted as having reached the area. They had built [[internment camps]] for the [[Old Horde]] survivors there, and had sealed the entry of the Tomb with two elven [[runestone]]s and numerous soldiers. *Thal'dranath was originally conceived and announced as a large island located to the southeast of the Broken Shore, which was to be featured in post-launch content for ''[[World of Warcraft: Legion|Legion]]''. It was planned to be an area dotted with ancient [[night elf]] ruins with a [[Burning Legion]] presence, but was scrapped during development in favor of more interesting ideas, as [[Blizzard Entertainment|Blizzard]] felt that the theme was already adequately explored in other zones on the Broken Isles.{{ref web|url=https://www.twitch.tv/warcraft/v/72784365?t=26m54s|title=Legion Live Developer Q&A w/ Ion Hazzikostas|date=2016-06-16|accessdate=2016-06-16}} Its name was later repurposed as the original [[Darnassian]] name for the Broken Shore. [[Zone Support - Thal'Dranath|A cut mission]] mentioned Thal'Dranath. **Thal'dranath still appears on in-game map objects. *Originally, the Broken Shore was going to be covered in dried coral to reflect that [[Gul'dan]] had raised it from the seafloor in the [[Second War]]. The art team later decided it was too serene and that it didn't scream "demon" enough, so they had the Legion devastate the island instead, remaking it as a solely demonic location.[http://www.wowhead.com/news=249821/blizzcon-2015-art-designer-interview-with-chris-robinson?refresh Interview with Chris Robinson] *[[Drak'thul]] can be found on the southern shore of the Broken Shore. *[[Jinyu]] ruins can be found underwater southeast of the [[Lost Temple]], past [[Acherus]]. *Northeast of the Tomb of Sargeras, there's an area of flora and sunken ships, its cargo, and a foundation of a building. *Before [[patch 7.2.0]] fleshed out the zone, the main-world Broken Shore was accessible but had almost no content other than patrols of level 110 elite demons. ==Gallery== ;Before Legionfall ([[patch 7.2.0]]): File:Broken Shore - Wrynn gunship.jpg|King Wrynn's [[Lion's Oath|fallen]] [[gunship]].
